request.deadline: 52-week contract period, with architecture assessment published by Q3 2027
deliverables: Compatible Daedalus releases at least 2 weeks before each mainnet hard fork
Continuous cardano-node and cardano-wallet integration and platform maintenance for Windows, macOS x86_64, macOS aarch64, and Linux
Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support in a stable release
CIP-30 dApp connector implementation in Daedalus with documentation
Ongoing English and Japanese user support and full Japanese translation for shipped features
Public architecture assessment with recommendation and resource estimates
request.recipient: Se7en Labs, Inc., with Intersect serving as administrator and milestone verifier
request.what: Daedalus Wallet maintenance and improvements for 2026-2027, including protocol maintenance, ecosystem expansion, user support, hardware wallet support, CIP-30, Japanese localisation, and architecture assessment.

claims.claim: Daedalus is Cardano's only full-node desktop wallet and derives wallet and governance data directly from the chain without third-party APIs or trusted backends.
Daedalus has approximately 4,000 monthly active users according to opt-in telemetry, while the proposer says the true count is meaningfully higher.
The proposal funds a time-and-materials engagement covering protocol maintenance, Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support, CIP-30 dApp connector work, Japanese localisation, and user support.
All funded outputs are described as public assets under the Apache License 2.0, including source code, build tooling, documentation, and release artifacts.

Se7en Labs says it assumed Daedalus responsibility under an IOG contract in January 2026 and shipped Mithril Snapshot Bootstrap, UTxO-HD/LSM backend integration, native Apple Silicon builds, a release CLI, and Nix build modernization.
The proposal says release-timing and version-currency success metrics are independently verifiable from public GitHub repositories and the Cardano mainnet chain.

The requested budget is 1,785,333 ADA, consisting of 1,666,667 ADA for maintenance and improvements, 33,333 ADA for test hardware, 33,333 ADA for financial audit, and 52,000 ADA for Intersect administration.
The proposer states that any unspent labor, hardware, or audit budget will be returned to the treasury.
The proposal states that Intersect will hold treasury funds in a dedicated account, verify milestones, and disburse funds monthly against verified work.
The proposer states the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit at the moment of submission.

summary: The document requests 1,785,333 ADA for a 52-week public-good maintenance and improvement engagement for Daedalus, administered by Intersect, with milestones for protocol compatibility, platform maintenance, hardware wallet support, CIP-30, Japanese localisation, support, and an architecture assessment.
